 Walnut Creek Property Owners Face Costly Tax Deadline 
 The first installment of property taxes becomes delinquent if not paid by Dec. 10. 
 Angela Woodall , Patch Staff 
 Posted Tue, Nov 17, 2026 at 1:07 pm PT CONTRA COSTA COUNTY, CA — Property owners have another December date to mark on their calendars and it's not one that comes with presents. 
 Property owners must pay the first installment of this year's property taxes by 5 p.m. on Dec. 10 to avoid a penalty. 
 Otherwise, they face a 10 percent penalty and an administrative cost will be added on to late second installment payments, according to the county.

 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . The second installment becomes delinquent if not paid by April 10, 2026.
 The deadlines apply across Concord, Walnut Creek, Lamorinda, and the rest of Contra Costa County.
 Find out what's happening in Walnut Creek for free with the latest updates from Patch. 
 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . The Contra Costa County Treasurer-Tax Collector’s Office accepts payments online, by phone, by mail, and in person.
 Owners who have not received a bill should call 925-608-9500 (a missing bill does not excuse late payment). Residents enrolled in paperless billing receive their bills by email.
 Owners can pay online through the tax portal or call 925-608-9500 to pay by phone. 
 PayPal, credit card, and debit card payments carry a 2.5% fee, with a $3.50 minimum. E-checks carry no service fee, but a rejected e-check may trigger a returned-check fee of up to $85.
 Owners paying by mail should send checks with installment coupons to P.O. Box 51104, Los Angeles, CA 90051. 
 Mailed payments must bear a U.S. Postal Service postmark before Dec. 1, to avoid penalties.
 The office accepts in-person payments at 625 Court St., Suite 100, Martinez, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. 
 A drive-thru check drop box on the building’s Main Street side operates around the clock until it closes at 5 p.m. Thursday, Dec. 10.
 The second installment is due Feb. 1, 2027. Because its April 10 delinquency date falls on a Saturday, the next-business-day rule shifts the deadline to 5 p.m. Monday, April 12. Late payment brings a 10% penalty and a $20 administrative charge.
 Owners may pay both installments together. Those mailing payment for the full bill must include both installment coupons.
 Owners can also sign up for paperless billing for email reminders and secure access.
 For more information, visit www.countytreasurer.org .
